# Preparation Functions

Reusable executable functions for preparing child documents, accepting supplied initialized publications, and tracking admission, selection and usability. A consuming clause supplies configuration, invocation bindings and domain rules. Callable functions do not by themselves establish a viewer’s permission or obligation.

## Configuration and inputs

Configuration comes through `connectionConfiguration`; its `parameters` default to `{}`. `configuredTemplate` uses `parameters.template` when present, otherwise `connectionSnapshots.template`.

- `bindings.parties` must be nonempty for preparation. It maps declared child parties using the executing document’s `/activation/parties`. `suppliedParties`, defaulting to `[]`, identifies roles to be supplied later.
- `obtain` defaults to `create` and accepts only `create` or `provide`. Creation rejects nonempty `suppliedParties`. Provision requires a nonempty `suppliedBy`, stored as `supplier` and later checked against `call/channel`.
- Omitting `prepareFor` selects internal mode `inherited`. An explicitly supplied value must be `bootstrap`; this requires `obtain: provide` and empty `inheritChannels`. Bootstrap preparation removes mapped lead and representative channels to permit fresh transports while retaining identity constraints. Its template must omit `/timelineAccess` and `/clauses/activation/parameters/accessPaths`. Preparation itself does not bootstrap or activate the child.
- `preparePublic` accepts `key`, `requestId`, `fields` and `values`. Its key fallback is `single`; `prepareKeyedPublic` requires an explicit nonempty key. Resolved keys and request identifiers must be nonempty text, and `requestId` defaults to the resolved key. `fields` and `values` default to `{}`.
- `fields` supplies top-level values permitted by `allowedFields`, excluding reserved structural and type-control names. `values` supplies named values mapped through `fieldPaths`; each target must contain a declaration against which the value validates. Targets must be non-root absolute pointers outside reserved control and identity roots.
- `specialization.dataPaths`, defaulting to `[]`, declares additional provider-fillable data slots. Each must identify an existing declaration, avoid reserved roots, and neither duplicate nor overlap another slot. Every party declared in the template is also a specialization slot.

`cardinality` and `destinationBinding` are read from `/clauses/<clauseKey>/type`. With `cardinality: single`, only key `single` is accepted and the destination is the binding named by `destinationBinding`. Otherwise the escaped key is appended to that destination. Host paths refer to the document where these functions execute, including a nested document’s own execution context.

Construction requires an uninitialized template and the required Activation clause. It records `creationIntent`, assigns `instanceKey` using the executing document’s initial identity, clause and key, and assigns related identities to existing uninitialized templates listed in `identityChildren`. In inherited mode, mapped preparation carries host access references and party transports into the child; conflicting destinations or transports are rejected. `inheritChannels` permits only supported explicit participant channels and rejects differing template declarations.

## Preparation and provision

`checkPreparation` freezes an `intent` containing configuration and template identities, `requestId`, `fields` and `values`. An existing entry with different intent is rejected as `PREPARATION_OBLIGATION_CONFLICT`; a new entry cannot occupy an existing destination.

`sharedPrepare` constructs the document, configures access and sources, obtains `domainTerms`, records specialization `slots`, and sets `requirementRef` to the prepared document’s identity. With `obtain: create`, it writes the prepared document at the destination and records `status: selected` and `documentOrigin`. With `obtain: provide`, it records `awaiting_provider` and emits `Document Provision Requested` for `suppliedBy`. Both paths emit `Document Prepared`. Preparation and selection do not establish initialization or usability.

`providePublic` accepts an existing publication in `document`, plus `inResponseTo` and `requirementRef`; `key` defaults to `single`. It requires an existing provision-mode entry, the configured supplier’s `call/channel`, and exact matches to the entry’s request and requirement references. Provision is rejected while status is `reapproval_required`, `admission_denied`, `cancelled` or `cancellation_requested`.

The supplied document must contain `/contracts/initialized/document`. Its initial document must match the reviewed preparation after permitted slot normalization. Its effective clause policy must also match: comparison retains clause `type`, `parameters`, `bindings`, and any `name` or `description`. Bootstrap normalization additionally permits the specified transport and access differences.

Both initial and current slot values undergo declaration validation. Current data-slot values must remain identical to their initialized originals. Party slots undergo identity checks; mapped roles receive additional checks, and bootstrap checks preserve specified actors and representative identities. Extra current party roles and changes to `/activation/required` are rejected. Bootstrap candidates must provide an initialized Timeline Access publication for every party and representative transport, with matching `/activation/accessPaths` and successful access validation. Finally, `domainValidateCandidate` must accept the candidate against frozen `domainTerms`.

A staged candidate records `candidateOrigin` and `candidateRef`. Its initial identity cannot subsequently be replaced. Staging produces:

- `admission_pending` when a `bindings.sources` mapping to `self` requires candidate parties absent from the host roster;
- `awaiting_activation` when the candidate’s `/activation/active` is not explicitly `true`;
- `linking` when required sources lack initialization, activity or roster coverage; a wrong source identity is rejected;
- `ready` when these staging checks pass.

Non-ready staging writes progress and emits `Document Admission Progress`. Ready provision writes the candidate publication reference at the destination, records `documentOrigin` and `selected`, and emits `Document Selected`. Replacing an already selected initial-document identity is forbidden.

Retry behavior is function-specific. `checkPreparation` recognizes identical intent as `duplicate`, but `preparePublic` still calls `sharedPrepare`, which writes preparation state and events. Likewise, `providePublic` does not short-circuit a `duplicate` result from its check. Duplicate detection alone therefore does not guarantee a side-effect-free public retry.

## Admission and cancellation

Admission requires configured `/clauses/activation/parameters/admission/approvers` and candidate access documents for the missing parties’ transports. The `admissionToken` binds the candidate and requirement identities, entry, activation revision, attempt, parties and access scope; `admissionRef` identifies that token. A changed token requires reapproval.

`nextAdmissionRequest` returns a grant proposal request when appropriate; it does not approve the proposal. It waits while a ledger proposal exists. Declined consent or an outdated activation revision can retire pending admission as `admission_denied` or `reapproval_required`, retaining the token, consents and reason and clearing a matching pending proposal.

`admissionInstallRequest` requires recorded approval history and a grant exactly matching the token. It can emit `Party Addition Requested` before all participant consents are present. That request carries access evidence; it neither grants private timeline access nor consents for anyone. Consent operations are installed on the proposed parties’ lead channels when access validation permits, with explicit `approve` or `decline` decisions and an `admissionRef`.

Installation readiness additionally requires every proposed party’s approval, the unchanged activation revision and valid combined access. The entry then becomes `installing`. `finishAdmission` requires that status and host roster coverage before recording `admittedRevision`, moving to `linking`, and emitting progress with status `admitted`.

`rebaseAdmissionPublic` requires `call/requireExactDocumentVersion: true`, a `call/channel` listed among admission approvers, the current `admissionRef`, and `reapproval_required`. It clears the token, reference and consents, increments `admissionAttempt`, retains the candidate identity, and returns the entry to `awaiting_provider`; its progress event says `reprovision_required`.

`cancelPublic` requires an existing entry without `documentOrigin`. It records `cancellation_requested` and emits `Preparation Cancellation Requested`; repeating that request returns `duplicate`. This is a cancellation request, not confirmed cancellation. Once a document is selected, cancellation must use domain-specific handling.

## State, sources and usability

Preparation entries live under `/process_<clauseKey>/entries`, indexed by the Blue identity of `key`. Each entry’s `itemPath` locates its state and `path` locates its destination. `prepared`, `intent`, `domainTerms` and `slots` retain the reviewed preparation. `requirementRef` identifies that preparation; `candidateRef` identifies a supplied publication; `candidateOrigin` and `documentOrigin` identify initial documents. `requestId` and event `inResponseTo` correlate work to the preparation request; `clauseId` and `itemKey` identify its clause and entry where emitted. Missing stored values do not imply a status, approval or configuration default.

`bindings.sources` maps every declared source alias to a document pointer or `self`. Configuration requires initialized, active sources matching their declarations, and records immutable source origins. A `self` requirement also records the child destination as `selectionPath`. Named mappings cannot coexist with nonempty legacy `sourcePaths`; legacy paths embed initialized source references. Construction reserves `documentAccess` and, when needed, `documentSources` clause names.

Inherited `bindSourcePublic` accepts `alias` and either `document` or `sourcePath`; a nonempty `sourcePath` takes precedence. Binding requires the declared origin, explicit source activity and roster validation. It cannot replace a different source origin. Binding a source does not change commercial approval requirements.

`sharedRefresh` examines selected entries whose destination exposes `/contracts/initialized/document`, rejecting changed initial identity. It records `usable` only when the selected document is explicitly active and `namedSourcesReady` passes. Each required source must be initialized, match its origin, be active and cover the child roster through lead-channel equality and reader-key checks. A nonempty source `selectionPath` must point back to an initialized document with the child’s origin. Failure of readiness returns status to `selected`; transition to `usable` emits `Document Attached`. If the destination lacks the initialized original, this refresh leaves that entry unchanged.

For usable entries, `domainNextActions` supplies `nextActions`; otherwise refresh uses an empty list. Changed action lists are stored and emitted with preparation correlation fields, and each emitted action’s `party` must be declared in the selected document. These descriptions do not execute or complete the described actions. Separately, `refreshSourceReadiness` records the executing document’s source readiness at `/sourceLinks/ready`.

Inherited access registration accepts 1–16 Timeline Access publications, requires exact-version review and a `call/channel` naming an activation party, then delegates installation. Separate inherited factory helpers `checkCreation` and `create` use `bindings.collection`, require keys without `/` or `~`, compare `creationIntent` at occupied destinations, and emit `Document Started` on creation.

## Domain hooks and outcomes

`domainPrepare` must return an object, `domainValidateCandidate` a boolean, and `domainNextActions` a list of at most 16 `Clause Response` descriptions. Their wrappers reject added changes or events and invalid result types. Configuration and domain hook bodies must be supplied by the consuming implementation; default source-declaration validators explicitly fail until specialized. Detailed mapping, party-identity, access-installation and consent-recording rules also depend on their helper implementations.

`acceptedNew` reports acceptance of the invoked work. It does not establish completed activation, admission, external action or cancellation.
